description: The hyperbolic metric on the unit disk provides a natural framework for Bloch functions: ||f||_B = sup (1-|z|^2)|f'(z)| ≤ 1 defines the Bloch class. The spectral gap of the Laplacian on the image domain f(D) constrains the geometry and covering radius. Spectral bounds from conformally flat manifold results could yield new geometric constraints on extremal domains.
mathematical_formalization: For Ω = f(D), λ_1(Ω) ≥ πj_{0,1}^2/|Ω|. If Ω ⊃ D(0,R), then λ_1(Ω) ≤ j_{0,1}^2/R^2. Combined with hyperbolic area bounds, this gives R ≤ Φ(||f||_B, λ_1).
analogical_connections: Heat kernel estimates on Riemannian manifolds
implementation_hypothesis: Compute Dirichlet eigenvalues of f(D) for families of Bloch functions using FEM. Derive chain of inequalities: spectral gap → area → covering radius → B_u bound.
experiment_seed: Compute Dirichlet eigenvalues of f(D) for f(z) = z/(1-z)^t using FreeFEM++. Track relationship between λ_1, Bloch norm, and maximal inscribed disk.
